brief.subject: Diesel dips to $6.292; FMCSA crackdown seen outlasting DC
brief.headline: Diesel eases 6 cents as FMCSA enforcement push looks set to stick
brief.dek: Diesel slips week over week, an industry CEO says the CDL crackdown will last, and a fraud report flags hacked communications in load theft.
brief.lede: Diesel averaged $6.292 per gallon, down 6.0 cents on the week but still up 9.3 cents over four weeks. Expect fuel to keep driving rates and surcharges.

sections.heading: Diesel Pulls Back, Still Elevated
bullets: $6.292 per gallon was the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-02, per EIA.
Down 6.0 cents (0.9%) from the prior week, a small break on fuel costs.
Up 9.3 cents over four weeks, so check that fuel surcharges still cover your real per-mile cost.
Fuel surcharges are driving most of this fall's intermodal contract increases, keeping rail pricing tied to diesel.

sections.heading: FMCSA Crackdown Expected to Stick
bullets: FreightWaves CEO Craig Fuller says big carriers are keeping FMCSA's enforcement push alive.
He argues non-domiciled CDL holders were probably the main reason the freight downturn dragged on.
His view: enforcement will outlast any political change in Washington, so keep compliance files tight.

sections.heading: Fraud: Hacked Comms Behind Theft
bullets: 40% of stolen loads were linked to compromised communications, according to a Highway fraud report.
Fraudulent calls surged 90%, so verify callers before acting on load or payment changes.
Carrier ownership reports more than doubled, pointing to more disputes over who controls an authority.

sections.heading: Border Lanes: Security and Trade
bullets: 826 National Guard officers will be deployed by Mexico to boost highway security, relevant to cross-border cargo safety.
1,000-plus pounds of meth turned up in a produce truck at the Texas border after a canine alert.
U.S. foreign-trade zones are pushing to fix USMCA tariff obstacles affecting cross-border freight.

sections.heading: Rail Shakeups Touch Drayage Work
bullets: Union Pacific's CEO said he'd raise rates on shippers opposing the Norfolk Southern merger; UP called it an offhand comment.
Schneider National is shifting its intermodal partnership to Norfolk Southern, which could reshape some ramp and drayage volumes.
